newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton ends barely higher in thin dealings.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton ends barely higher in thin dealings.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures ended tightly mixed in thin volume as players awaited news from Thursday's weekly export and sales data and a monthly consumption report.
Market sources expect the export and sales data to reflect brisk business of about 125,000 bales for the week. The consumption data should have no influence over prices, however.
"Consumption could be slightly down from last month but it should be a non-event," a trader said. "We're just in the summer doldrums."
Volume was estimated at 5,000 lots compared with Tuesday's official 5,688 lots.
The benchmark December contract ended 0.03 cent higher at 74.61 cents a lb, having ranged from 74.77 to 74.30 cents. The rest of the board settled 0.10 higher to 0.20 cent lower.
While players look toward the U.S. Department of Agriculture's August estimates some analysts say the data will not give an accurate picture of how the crop is developing.

Sharon Johnson, an analyst with Frank Schneider and Co Inc, said that because the crop is running about three weeks behnid schedule, the report will provide a picture of the crop as if it were the second week in July, not early August.
"The report is not going to give us the kind of concrete answers we want," Johnson said. "August will help but I wouldn't bet the farm on it."
